Stay quiet, accept punishment for something you didn't do, and feel miserable.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Communicates the truth calmly and assertively without escalating conflict.

payoffOriginal.prompt: A friend screams at you when you don't want to share your candy bar. What do you do?
options: Say: "I get mad when you scream at me because this is my snack. Please ask nicely next time."
Yell back at them and throw the candy bar at their face.
Give them the candy bar silently while feeling resentful inside.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Sets personal boundaries using Power Talk without losing self-control.

payoffOriginal.prompt: A friend tells you that she's not inviting you to her party Friday night. What do you do?
options: Say: "When you tell me I'm not invited, I feel left out. I need for you to be honest with me about why."
Yell that her party will be stupid anyway and tell everyone not to go.
Pretend you don't care, go home, and cry by yourself.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Expresses hurt feelings constructively without attacking the other person.

payoffOriginal.prompt: Another student is telling your best friend not to hang around with you. What do you do?
options: Speak to them: "I get mad when you tell my friend not to hang around with me because it's hurtful. Please stop."
Confront the student aggressively and threaten them.
Avoid both of them and assume you lost your best friend.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Addresses rumors directly using Power Talk rather than resorting to aggression.

payoffOriginal.prompt: A good friend tells your deepest secret to another friend. What do you do?
options: Say: "When you tell my secrets, I feel betrayed. I need for you to keep private things to yourself."
Tell an embarrassing secret about them to the entire class as revenge.
Ignore them completely and end the friendship without explaining why.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Addresses trust issues clearly rather than seeking harmful revenge.

payoffOriginal.prompt: The boy sitting behind you is constantly poking you in the back wanting to ask you questions. What do you do?
options: Turn around: "When you poke me, I feel distracted. I need for you to stop poking and raise your hand."
Grab his pencil, yell at him, and throw it across the room.
Ignore it, get increasingly frustrated, and fail to focus on your work.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Sets immediate classroom boundaries without causing a disruption.

payoffOriginal.prompt: Others are teasing you about your new haircut. What do you do?
options: Say: "I get mad when you tease me about my hair because it hurts. Please stop talking about it."
Make fun of their appearance in return and start an insult contest.
Put your hood up, hide your face, and feel terrible all day.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Stops teasing assertively without sinking to the level of the teasers.

payoffOriginal.prompt: The other team is cheating. What do you do?
options: Pause the game: "When you break the rules, I feel frustrated. I need for us to play fairly."
Accuse them of being cheaters, shove a player, and ruin the game.
Keep playing silently while knowing it's unfair and lose on purpose.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Addresses fairness constructively while keeping sportsmanship intact.

payoffOriginal.prompt: You get in trouble for coming home late. What do you do?
options: Say: "I'm sorry. When I lose track of time, I understand why you worry. I need to set an alarm next time."
Slam your door, scream at your parents, and argue that it's not a big deal.
Go to your room silently, pout, and refuse to speak to anyone for days.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Demonstrates accountability and proactive problem-solving.

payoffOriginal.prompt: The librarian tells you that you are making too much noise in the library. What do you do?
options: Say: "When I talk loudly, I realize it disrupts others. I need to lower my voice right away."
Argue that you weren't being loud and accuse the librarian of picking on you.
Roll your eyes, slump down in your chair, and stop working entirely.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Accepts feedback politely and corrects the behavior immediately.

payoffOriginal.prompt: Other kids call you an "easy out" during the ball game. What do you do?
options: Say: "I get mad when you call me names because it's unsportsmanlike. Please focus on the game."
Throw your bat down, insult them back, or refuse to leave the base.
Walk off the field in tears and quit playing for the rest of recess.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: De-escalates trash-talk calmly while maintaining personal composure.

payoffOriginal.prompt: A classmate accidentally runs into you and knocks you down. What do you do?
options: Get up and say: "When you run into me, I feel startled. I need for you to watch where you go next time."
Push them down to get revenge and yell at them for being clumsy.
Stay on the ground, say nothing, and hold a grudge for the rest of the day.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Distinguishes between accidents and intentional actions calmly.

payoffOriginal.prompt: Your mother puts you on restriction for not doing the dishes or taking out the garbage. What do you do?
options: Do the chores, then say: "I understand why you're upset. I need to remember my chores so I don't lose privileges."
Yell at your mom, throw a fit, and refuse to do the chores at all.
Do the chores silently while slamming items around and sulking.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Takes ownership of personal responsibilities without escalating argument.

payoffOriginal.prompt: Another student cuts in front of you in the lunch line. What do you do?
options: Say: "I get mad when you cut in line because everyone has been waiting. Please go to the back."
Push them out of the way and scream at them to move.
Let them cut in front of you without saying a word and complain later.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Asserts your place in line firmly without resorting to physical conflict.

payoffOriginal.prompt: Your best friend tells you that you have been acting like a snob lately. What do you do?
options: Say: "When you say that, I feel surprised. I need for you to give me an example so I can understand."
Yell at them, tell them they are a bad friend, and walk away.
Ignore the comment, stop talking to them, and feel resentful.
payoffOriginal.teachingPoint: A: Invites open communication and clarification to resolve friendship issues.

payoffModern.prompt: Someone leaves you out of a group chat with all your close friends. What do you do?
options: Talk to a friend privately: "When I see a group chat without me, I feel left out. I need for you to let me know if there's a reason."
Post public status updates calling everyone fake friends and starting drama.
Mute everyone, delete the app, and silently stop talking to all your friends.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Expresses feeling excluded constructively without turning it into public drama.

payoffModern.prompt: A classmate posts an embarrassing photo of you on social media without asking. What do you do?
options: Send a private message: "When you post pictures of me without asking, I feel uncomfortable. I need for you to take it down."
Post an even more embarrassing picture of them in revenge to humiliate them.
Ignore it while feeling miserable and hope people stop looking at it.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Sets boundaries on digital privacy assertively without retaliating.

payoffModern.prompt: A teammate intentionally throws or ruins an online multiplayer match you are playing. What do you do?
options: Mute your mic and say after: "When you throw the game, I feel frustrated. I need for us to play as a team."
Scream into your microphone, insult their skill, and rage-quit the game.
Keep playing quietly while getting furious, then rage-quit without saying a word.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Protects your composure and uses mute tools instead of feeding toxic behavior.

payoffModern.prompt: A friend ghosted you after you made plans to hang out over the weekend. What do you do?
options: Message them: "When you don't show up or reply, I feel disrespected. I need for you to tell me if plans change."
Spam their phone with 50 angry texts and block them on everything.
Pretend nothing happened and wait for them to contact you whenever they feel like it.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Addresses accountability and communication standards in a friendship directly.

payoffModern.prompt: A classmate takes credit for your section of a digital slide presentation. What do you do?
options: Politely clarify in class: "When you present my slides, I feel overlooked. I need to present the work I completed."
Interrupt loudly, call them a thief in front of the class, and demand the teacher punish them.
Let them take the grade for your work while feeling resentful toward them.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Reclaims credit for your work calmly and professionally.

payoffModern.prompt: A friend reads your private direct messages over your shoulder without permission. What do you do?
options: Cover your screen: "When you look at my phone, I feel like my privacy isn't respected. I need for you to ask first."
Snatch their phone out of their hand, start digging through their texts, and yell at them.
Tilt your phone away silently, feeling uncomfortable but saying nothing.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Establishes physical and digital boundaries firmly.

payoffModern.prompt: Someone removes you from a shared class project folder without telling you. What do you do?
options: Ask the group: "When I get removed from the folder, I feel confused. I need to stay in the folder so I can do my part."
Delete all shared files out of anger so no one can complete the project.
Assume they hate you, do no work, and take a failing grade silently.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Solves technical and social misunderstandings directly to protect your grade.

payoffModern.prompt: A friend spoils the ending of a new movie or game online after you asked them not to. What do you do?
options: Say: "When you spoil the ending, I feel disappointed because I asked you not to. Please keep spoilers to yourself."
Post angry comments spoiling things they care about and block them immediately.
Unfollow them silently and hold a grudge for weeks without explaining why.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Communicates boundaries clearly when someone disregards your simple requests.

payoffModern.prompt: Someone sends you an unkind comment or insult in an online game lobby. What do you do?
options: Mute/report them, then say: "When you use insults, I feel annoyed. I need to play in a positive lobby."
Type back nasty insults, start a flame war, and get yourself reported.
Leave the game crying and avoid playing your favorite game ever again.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Uses built-in moderation tools (mute/report) to maintain self-control.

payoffModern.prompt: Your parents activate screen-time limits on your phone right while you are texting a friend. What do you do?
options: Talk to them in person: "When my screen time turns off mid-text, I feel stressed. I need a 5-minute warning next time."
Slam your door, scream at your parents, and demand they unlock the phone.
Sulk in your room, refuse to eat dinner, and give everyone the silent treatment.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Negotiates household tech rules respectfully without escalating conflict.

payoffModern.prompt: A friend forwards a private voice note or text you sent them to someone else. What do you do?
options: Say: "When you forward my private messages, I feel betrayed. I need for what I share with you to stay private."
Forward their personal secrets to a giant group chat as payback.
Stop trusting them completely but act like everything is fine when you see them.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Addresses breached trust directly using Power Talk.

payoffModern.prompt: Others leave mean jokes in the comment section of a video or photo you posted. What do you do?
options: Delete the comments, block the users, and tell a trusted adult if it continues.
Respond with harsh personal insults to every mean commenter to defend yourself.
Delete your entire account, go to bed upset, and refuse to talk to anyone.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Takes control of your digital space by removing toxic interactions.

payoffModern.prompt: A classmate copies your homework online and submits it right before you do. What do you do?
options: Speak to the teacher: "When my work is copied, I feel concerned about my grade. I need to clarify that this is my original work."
Confront the classmate in the hallway, shove them, and start a fight.
Do nothing and risk getting a zero for cheating alongside them.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Protects academic integrity through proper reporting channels.

payoffModern.prompt: Your gaming group replaces you with someone else for a weekend tournament. What do you do?
options: Say to the team leader: "When I get replaced without notice, I feel let down. I need to know why I was swapped out."
Spam their social pages with hate messages and ruin their live stream.
Quit the team discord server immediately and pretend you never cared about gaming.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Seeks direct clarity and feedback instead of reacting out of hurt pride.

payoffModern.prompt: Someone screenshots an embarrassing text you sent and shares it in a class channel. What do you do?
options: Contact the moderator or teacher: "When private texts are posted in class channels, I feel harassed. I need this removed."
Threaten the person who shared it and start an aggressive online feud.
Log off, refuse to go to school the next day, and hide in your room.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Uses appropriate authority figures to handle online harassment.

payoffModern.prompt: A friend takes your unlocked phone and posts a joke status on your profile without asking. What do you do?
options: Delete the post and say: "When you post from my account, I feel annoyed. I need for you to leave my phone alone."
Take their phone, throw it on the ground, or post something malicious on their profile.
Laugh along uncomfortably while secretly feeling angry and violated.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Sets firm personal boundaries regarding digital devices.

payoffModern.prompt: Classmates start recording a prank on you for social media without your permission. What do you do?
options: Look at the camera calmly: "When you film me without asking, I feel uncomfortable. I need you to stop recording now."
Smash their phone out of their hand, start a physical fight, and curse at them.
Duck your head, run away crying, and hide in the bathroom for the rest of recess.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Asserts your right to consent and privacy calmly on camera.

payoffModern.prompt: A friend promises to join your online gaming squad, but ditches you for a higher-ranked group. What do you do?
options: Say: "When you ditch our squad after promising, I feel disappointed. I need you to be reliable when we make plans."
Join their game session, disrupt their match, and call them names over game chat.
Play alone in silence while feeling bitter and refuse to invite them ever again.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Addresses reliability and respect in friendships directly.

payoffModern.prompt: Someone unfollows or blocks you online after a minor disagreement in class. What do you do?
options: Talk to them at school: "When you block me over a minor issue, I feel confused. I need for us to talk things out."
Create fake accounts to stalk their profile and leave angry messages on their posts.
Block them back on everything, tell people they are dead to you, and hold a lifelong grudge.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Prefers face-to-face communication over digital stonewalling.

payoffModern.prompt: A group project partner doesn't do any work on a shared presentation and expects you to cover. What do you do?
options: Say: "When you don't complete your slides, I feel overwhelmed. I need for you to finish your assigned part today."
Do all their work, but put insults about them on the final slide for the teacher to see.
Do all their work silently, let them get an 'A' for free, and complain to your parents later.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Holds group members accountable before project deadlines pass.

payoffModern.prompt: Someone spreads a false rumor about you on a school messaging server. What do you do?
options: Address the server admin/teacher: "When false rumors are posted here, I feel unsafe. I need this post removed."
Start spreading even worse lies about that person to ruin their reputation.
Delete your app, stay silent, and let everyone believe the lie.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Uses official reporting systems to deal with defamation effectively.

payoffModern.prompt: Your teacher confiscates your phone because a friend kept texting you during class. What do you do?
options: Hand over the phone, then text your friend later: "When you text during class, I get in trouble. Please wait until lunch."
Yell at the teacher, refuse to hand over your phone, and storm out of the classroom.
Give up the phone angrily, pout all day, and blame the teacher for being unfair.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Respects classroom rules while addressing the root cause with your friend.

payoffModern.prompt: A friend demands your account password or unlock code to prove you trust them. What do you do?
options: Say: "When you demand my passwords, I feel pressured. I need for you to trust me without having my account info."
Give them your password, but secretly log into their accounts to spy on them too.
Give them all your passwords out of fear they won't be your friend anymore.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Protects account security and personal independence in relationships.

payoffModern.prompt: Someone turns a picture of your face into a mean meme and sends it around. What do you do?
options: Report the image: "When my photo is turned into a meme, I feel disrespected. I need this image deleted immediately."
Make a meaner meme targeting their family members and blast it to everyone.
Pretend to laugh at it so people think you don't care, even though you are hurt inside.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Rejects cyberbullying assertively through proper channels without lowering your standards.

payoffModern.prompt: A friend gets angry and spam-calls you when you take an hour to reply to a text. What do you do?
options: Say: "When you spam-call me, I feel overwhelmed. I need you to understand I am not always at my phone."
Yell at them over the phone, call them needy, and block their number for a week.
Apologize repeatedly, feel guilty for having a life offline, and promise to reply in seconds next time.
payoffModern.teachingPoint: A: Sets healthy boundaries around text response time and personal availability.
